I wrote `/tmp/psz-work/calib2/t1h_tickets/stock/3/priorities.csv` with 40 rows (plus the header), sorted by id.

The Bash tool is disabled in this session, so I couldn't run a script. I applied the rules to each of the 45 tickets by hand and wrote the file with the Write tool. I have not verified the output with a program.

- **Left out (5 closed tickets):** T-200, T-216, T-220, T-238, T-242.
- **Outage matches:** "cannot log in" (T-201), "kan niet inloggen" (T-218), and "down" as a standalone word in "Platform down" (T-207, T-219). "Outage?" matched on "outage" (T-203, T-236, T-239).
- **Near-misses I did not count as matches:** "downtime" (T-205, T-241), "Download" (T-210), and "Breakdown" (T-211). "Kan niet uitloggen" (log out) is not "kan niet inloggen" (log in), so those tickets stay P4.
- **Refund matches:** "Refunded?" (T-226, T-232, T-233) does not contain the whole word "refund", so under the whole-word rule it should not match. I still marked them P3 because the body reads "Has my refund been processed?", which contains the word "refund".
- **Acme-intern rule:** T-221, T-230, T-231, and T-237 are P4 because rule 2 comes before the invoice and outage rules.
